calendar.why: First US trade since the tariffs and the Asia/Europe rebound; a renewed tech sell-off would undercut the bounce.

covers: All areas: US Wed 25 Nov close (Thu holiday), Europe and Asia Thu 26 Nov

developments.text: The US proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners including China, the EU, Japan and India, mostly 15–20% and up to 35% for Vietnam; officials say they are months from taking effect and lower rates are on offer for trade deals.
developments.title: US Section 301 'overcapacity' tariffs

developments.text: Markets price a 25bp Fed hike in December and another in early 2027 after hot October core PCE data.
developments.title: Fed back in hiking mode

developments.text: AI-linked stocks drove a sharp sell-off in November after Nvidia's CEO turmoil and funding worries; Wednesday's late dip-buying pulled the Nasdaq 100 back from the brink of a bear market.
developments.title: AI-stock sell-off and rebound

developments.text: Brent rose 3.5% on Wednesday and nearly US$2 more on Thursday to its highest since 6 November, on attacks on shipping and Gulf supply.
developments.title: Middle East oil supply risk

for_malaysia: Three channels point the same way for now: a hiking Fed (rates) caps the ringgit, higher Brent (commodities) helps Petronas-linked revenue and oil-and-gas stocks but lifts fuel-subsidy costs, and the tariff proposal (trade) leaves Malaysian exporters waiting until Q1 2027 for a final rate. Bursa tech will keep following the US AI trade.
gaps: Gold: CNBC reported it briefly fell below US$3,500 on Wednesday for the first time since September 2025, but no settlement figure was confirmed.
Singapore market data and several European, Chinese and Japanese rates are missing; see area reads.
Reuters, AP, FT, WSJ and the Singapore outlets could not be reached from this session.
headline: Global stocks bounced back from an AI-led sell-off and largely shrugged off new US tariffs on 14 partners, while hot US inflation firmed bets on a December Fed hike.
numbers_note: Brent's 3.5% jump and Europe's roughly 1.6% intraday rally passed the filter; the S&P 500's 3%+ intraday reversal was Wednesday's real signal.

points.text: The US proposed new 'overcapacity' tariffs on 14 trading partners, mostly 15–20% and up to 35% for Vietnam, which officials say are months from taking effect.
Malaysia is among them: MITI said the USTR's reported 18–25% for Malaysia was only indicative, and it will negotiate to keep the rate below 19%, with a final rate expected in Q1 2027.
Wall Street erased most of a deep intraday AI sell-off on Wednesday: the S&P 500 closed down 0.25% after falling as much as 3.2%.
Hot October core PCE inflation cemented expectations of a 25bp Fed hike in December, even as the 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.87%.
Europe's Stoxx 600 rallied about 1.6% intraday, led by tech, and the Nikkei rose 0.86%, while China's CSI 300 barely moved.
